nodes.title: Colour echoes by distance from the selected verse
nodes.body:
<!-- status -->
**Waiting on:** Danyel, since 2026-11-21T01:03:40.299Z
**Ask:** 
**To test:** Echoes view: pin a verse (II Kings 22:1) and check the four distance colours and the legend
<!-- status-data {"v":1,"waitingOn":"owner","since":"2026-11-21T01:03:40.299Z","ask":"","questions":[],"toTest":"Echoes view: pin a verse (II Kings 22:1) and check the four distance colours and the legend","writtenAt":"2026-11-21T01:03:40.299Z","fingerprint":"6572b39f"} -->
<!-- /status -->

The Echoes view coloured each verse by a colour wheel laid over the map, which was hard to read. It now colours by how far each echo is from the selected verse.

**What it does**
- Four steps, near to far: same chapter, same book, same section of the Tanakh (Torah / Prophets / Writings), another section. Kings I/II, Samuel I/II, Chronicles I/II, Ezra/Nehemiah and the Twelve Minor Prophets each count as one book. Ramp is plasma-like, near dark and far light: chapter (0.54, 0.19, 300), book (0.64, 0.22, 350), section (0.84, 0.15, 50), another section (0.96, 0.1, 95) in OKLCH.
- Verse selected (pinned or hovered): the verse is white, its echoes take their distance colour, other verses with echoes are dimmed grey, the rest are plain grey.
- Nothing selected: each verse with echoes takes the colour of its farthest echo.
- Plain grey squares keep their usual light-and-dark pattern at 0.6 of its brightness in this view only, so the palest step stands out. The pattern is not narrowed.
- The legend lists the four steps; the card summary shows four swatches (the labelled version was too wide on a phone).
- Removed with the wheel: the wheel itself, the section strips in the legend, and the shell's backdrop layer (`backdrop.ts`, the `backdrop` overlay hook, its test), which only the wheel used. `wheel.ts` became `places.ts`, keeping only the reading order.

Closes #606
Closes #494 (the wheel was a backdrop that popped in; both the wheel and the backdrop are gone)

**Choices Danyel did not settle**
- Ezra/Nehemiah counted as one book, as in the prototype; the issue named only Kings, Chronicles and the minor prophets (and the brief Samuel).
- The ramp colours are the prototype's OKLCH values as given; some channels fall just outside sRGB and clip, as they did in the prototype pictures.

**To look at** on the branch preview https://echo-distance-606-torahmap.danyel.workers.dev/ : `?overlay=text-analytics&analysis=echoes` at rest, then pin a verse such as II Kings 22:1 or I Kings 16:27 and hover others.

Checks: typecheck, `npm test`, layout suite (the echoes states pass on desktop, tablet and phone).

nodes.title: Colour search terms by hashing the word, from six hues
nodes.body:
<!-- status -->
**Waiting on:** Danyel, since 2026-11-20T18:31:11.261Z
**Ask:** Back to the original nine colours, as you asked. A new box gets a random free colour and keeps it while you type; a word arriving from a link or story gets its hashed colour
**Questions:**
1. A typed word may come back in a different colour after a reload or a shared link, since links carry no colour.  (**leave it** | carry each term's colour in the link)
**To test:** 1) Search two words and check neither changes colour as you type 2) reload: colours may change (the question) 3) Open the Tour stop with Jacob: his name should be orange, as the story now says
<!-- status-data {"v":1,"waitingOn":"owner","since":"2026-11-20T18:31:11.261Z","ask":"Back to the original nine colours, as you asked. A new box gets a random free colour and keeps it while you type; a word arriving from a link or story gets its hashed colour","questions":[{"n":1,"text":"A typed word may come back in a different colour after a reload or a shared link, since links carry no colour.","choices":["leave it","carry each term's colour in the link"],"defaultChoice":"leave it"}],"toTest":"1) Search two words and check neither changes colour as you type 2) reload: colours may change (the question) 3) Open the Tour stop with Jacob: his name should be orange, as the story now says","writtenAt":"2026-11-20T18:31:11.261Z","fingerprint":"1267845a"} -->
<!-- /status -->

## The problem

A search term's colour depended only on how many terms came before it: the first was always blue, the second always orange. Danyel asked for the colour to come from the word instead.

## What changed

**The palette is unchanged from main**: the same nine hues, in the same order, at the same lightness and chroma cap.

**Colour from the word.** The term's text is lowercased and stripped of vowel points and punctuation (the same `plainName` the picks use), hashed (FNV-1a), and taken mod 9. If that colour is held by another term or a pick, it steps to the next in the list. So "Abraham" and "abraham" agree, and a word's colour depends on what else is on the map only when there is a clash.

**When it is chosen.** Chosen once, when the term is made, and kept until it is removed; typing never changes it. A box the reader opens to type in gets a random free colour. A term that arrives with its word (a link, a story stop, a comma-split word) gets the hashed colour, so links and stops always show the same colours. Removing a term recolours nobody else.

**Picks share the palette.** The limits are as on main: at most five terms and four picks, so together they never exceed the nine colours and a colour is always left. Picks and terms also refuse to be added when no free colour remains.

**Other places.** The IEEE VIS story swatches for search terms now read each term's real colour. In the tour, Jacob's name now lands on the orange rather than the pink, so the story text says "in orange". The EU AI Act ring test finds the search's colour from the palette instead of expecting a fixed cyan.

Tests check behaviour (same word, same colour whatever the case or order; a clash takes the next free; terms and picks never share) and assert no specific colours.

## What to look at

Preview: https://620-term-colours-torahmap.danyel.workers.dev. Search a word, then the same word in another case, then the tour stop "Jacob's name, in orange".

![explore-search--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/ba2d38f1522d91535f158ce2e1d243b74951ba7c/explore-search--desktop.png?raw=true)
![explore-search--phone](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/ba2d38f1522d91535f158ce2e1d243b74951ba7c/explore-search--phone.png?raw=true)
![explore-search-and-overlay--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/ba2d38f1522d91535f158ce2e1d243b74951ba7c/explore-search-and-overlay--desktop.png?raw=true)

Closes #620

nodes.title: Better camera motion: one flight path for every glide
nodes.body:
<!-- status -->
**Waiting on:** Danyel, since 2026-11-20T09:23:12.020Z
**Ask:** 
<!-- status-data {"v":1,"waitingOn":"owner","since":"2026-11-20T09:23:12.020Z","ask":"","questions":[],"toTest":null,"writtenAt":"2026-11-20T18:39:52.905Z","fingerprint":"6572b39f"} -->
<!-- /status -->

Closes #605

Every camera move that is not the reader's own hands now goes through one function, `planGlide` (`packages/engine/src/glide.ts`), driven by `animateCameraTo`. Hit stepping, Go to, the overlay panels' travel, the left and right arrows (which used to jump, and now slide at the zoom you have), and the story's rejoin and phone-swipe eases all use it. `centerOnItem` is gone.

- **Long moves** rise, pan and descend (van Wijk and Nuij's flight), so you see where you are going instead of a blur.
- **Moves of about a screen-width or less** are an eased pan at a steady zoom.
- **Longer moves take longer**, from 300 ms up to 2 s.
- **Flattening rule:** the camera never rises until it sees more than 0.75 times the distance it travels, so a middling move stays low while a long one still rises.
- **Interrupting:** a move that starts while another is running eases out only, so a held arrow key keeps moving.
- **Reduced motion:** every camera move snaps.

All the numbers are named constants at the top of `glide.ts` (`FLIGHT_*`, `PAN_WITHIN_WIDTHS`).

## What to look at

On the preview: search a word and click through hits far apart; Go to "I Chronicles 1:1" from Genesis 1:1 (long) and "Isaiah 40:1" from "Psalms 23:1" (medium); pin a verse and hold the left or right arrow. Frames below are the real app at 24 fps, stepped on a fixed clock (software WebGL), not a live recording.

Long, Genesis 1:1 to I Chronicles 1:1 (1.6 s, rises to zoom 0.57):
![long](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/9b26fb09d67111d1347649f44aa1672e39cf8564/filmstrip-long.png?raw=true)

Medium, Psalms 23:1 to Isaiah 40:1 (1.4 s, rises to zoom 0.79):
![mid](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/9b26fb09d67111d1347649f44aa1672e39cf8564/filmstrip-mid.png?raw=true)

Short, Genesis 1:1 to 3:5 (300 ms, no zoom change):
![short](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/9b26fb09d67111d1347649f44aa1672e39cf8564/filmstrip-short.png?raw=true)

Videos: [long](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/9b26fb09d67111d1347649f44aa1672e39cf8564/long.mp4?raw=true), [mid](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/9b26fb09d67111d1347649f44aa1672e39cf8564/mid.mp4?raw=true), [short](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/9b26fb09d67111d1347649f44aa1672e39cf8564/short.mp4?raw=true).

## Not changed

The story's scroll-driven blend between stops (`controller.ts`) and Back/Forward and links, which set the camera outright, are as before. The rejoin and swipe durations (700 ms, 1500 ms) are unchanged since the colour blend shares them, so they do not shorten under reduced motion.

## Checks

Typecheck, all unit tests, `npm run test:browser` (541 passed). Unit tests cover the path (ends match, never below the zoom floor, short moves keep their zoom, rise capped by distance, duration grows within limits, interrupting starts moving at once, reduced motion snaps).

**Answers from PR Board**

How does it look? → **looks good, prep for merge**

Reviewed up to `6aee466`

Two reviews of the rebased branch: one fresh read for duplication and drift, one for bugs.

- The story's rejoin eased the camera twice: once with the story's curve, then again inside the glide. The camera lagged the colour change (at a quarter of the way, the camera had made 0.2% of its trip and the picture 12.5%). Fixed in `7e4a8d3`: the glide gets the raw progress, and the picture keeps the story's curve.
- `FLIGHT_MIN_ZOOM = 0.1` was a copy of the Tanakh's zoom floor. Talmud's floor is 0.05 and VIS's is 0.08. Fixed in `7e4a8d3`: the glide reads `link.zoom.min` from the text, so a long flight on Talmud can now rise to 0.05.
- A map with no width yet (hidden, or not yet laid out) made the rejoin compute NaN cameras. Fixed in `7e4a8d3`: with no width the glide falls back to a plain pan, and a test covers it.
- The highest point of the flight was counted even when it fell outside the path, so the flattening loop flattened a little more than it needed to. Fixed in `7e4a8d3`.
- The `gliding` flag repeated what `stopCameraGlide` already says. Fixed in `7e4a8d3`: `onDone` clears the stop function, and the code checks that instead.
- Comments trimmed in `7e4a8d3`. The "every camera move goes through here" line is now in one place (`glideTo`).
- Ease curves "written twice": declined. The engine's existing curves are quadratic and the glide's are cubic, so they are different functions, not copies.
- The rejoin plans a new path every frame, so if the reader scrolls during a rejoin and the target crosses the one-screen-width line, the path switches from a pan to a flight and the camera jumps. Declined for now. It needs a reader scrolling mid-rejoin, and planning once would leave the camera aiming at an old target.
- Plan the pan case before building the flight path, to skip the work: declined. The saving is tiny and the code would get longer.
- Tuning constants exported only for tests: declined. The tests read the duration limits from them instead of repeating the numbers.

Unit tests (3248), typecheck and the layout browser suite (541 passed) pass at `7e4a8d3`.

Reviewed up to `7e4a8d3`

Read the fix commit; each change does what the comment above says, and nothing else changed. No new findings.

Reviewed up to `7e4a8d3`

- Rejoin eased camera and picture on two curves: fixed in 0327956; the glide takes already-eased progress and the rejoin feeds one eased value to both.
- Easing functions beside `easingFunctions`: fixed in 0327956; they now live only in `animateCameraTo`, which owns the move's easing.
- Rejoin replans every frame: declined; its target (the story camera) moves as the reader scrolls, so a plan made once would be wrong.
- Reduced motion handled two ways: declined; the camera option and the colour fade are different mechanisms, and each is tested.
- Six exported constants: fixed in 0327956; only the ones the test reads are still exported.
- Magic numbers in the flattening loop: fixed in 0327956, now named.
- Prose: false `glideTo` docstring, restating comments, long `planGlide` docstring: fixed in 0327956.
- `glideToCentre` single-use wrapper: fixed in 0327956, inlined.
- Missing test for a path stopping at the rho floor: declined; the zoom-floor test covers the flattened path.
- Correctness review: no bugs found.

Reviewed up to `0327956`

Read the fix commit after the first round: mechanical (easing moved into `animateCameraTo`, constants named, comments trimmed). Typecheck, `npm test` and the layout browser suite pass. Nothing further found.
🤖 Claude: prep for merge

Reviewed up to `71b6377`

Lead's follow-up on the rejoin: the camera and picture already share one eased value (0327956); the plan is rebuilt each frame because the story's target camera moves as the reader scrolls (the code comment says so). Reduced motion was ignored by the rejoin and the phone page-swipe ease: fixed in 71b6377, both now snap (duration 0). Typecheck, `npm test` and the layout browser suite pass. Nothing further found.
🤖 Claude: prep for merge

nodes.title: Haftarah: a reading with two passages is coloured across the gap between them
nodes.body:
Danyel noticed while trying the pinned-reading card in #628: lighting **Tzav** colours the whole area in Jeremiah, though its Ashkenazi haftarah is two passages with a gap between them (Jeremiah 7:21–8:3 and 9:22–23, as `public/data/overlays/haftarah/mappings.json` has it). The data holds the gap; something between the data and the map spans it. Other readings with more than one passage are probably affected too.

🤖 Claude: filed from Danyel's report.

<!-- status -->
**Waiting on:** nobody, since 2026-11-21T01:03:29.907Z
**Ask:**

🤖 Claude: working on this in branch `632-haftarah-gaps`.

🤖 Claude: the ranges are right. Tzav's Ashkenazi haftarah gives exactly Jeremiah 7:21–8:3 and 9:22–23. The gap is filled because lighting a reading also lights every reading that shares a verse with it (`litByPreview` in `apps/tanakh/src/overlays/haftarah.ts`, pinned by the test "lights every reading that shares a verse with the previewed one"). Tisha B'Av Morning (Jeremiah 8:13–9:23) shares 9:22–23, so its whole passage lights up in its own colour, gap included. Open question for Danyel: keep that, or light only the chosen reading's own verses? The fix touches code #628 also edits, so it would come after #628.

nodes.title: explore: colors more diverse
nodes.body:
right now, the first search I show is always blue ,the second always orange. feels inelegant... and loses some of the beauty. imagining things like:
* the search is some hash(text), with collision avoidance (so it chains, or picks the next available color off the lsit)

Not sure how that would feel, but especailly for IEEEVIS mpa, we KEPT coming back to the same view -- blue dots on grey screen
